query: What patient needs appear in visit notes?

per_column.name: identified_patient_needs
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by extracting a multi-label taxonomy of patient needs from the notes -- strong grouping/comparison axis. Most row samples are well grounded (MI follow-up -> med mgmt/diagnostic/monitoring; acne -> med/skin care). However the annual physical exam row is tagged 'pain_management' despite the text explicitly denying pain and describing a routine exam; it also omits preventive_care which the text clearly warrants. This is a confident, contradicted label, so groundedness is only moderate.

per_column.name: needs_count
per_column.rationale: A useful aggregate for measuring visit complexity and distributing analysis. It is a direct deterministic function of the extracted needs, so it inherits their groundedness; where the underlying labels err (e.g. spurious pain flag) the count is inflated, but as a derivation it is sound.

per_column.name: needs_pain_management
per_column.rationale: A binary indicator giving a clean per-need axis to filter/model on. The knee-injury row is correctly flagged, but the annual-physical row is flagged 1 despite the note denying chest pain and describing no pain complaint -- a clear unsupported assertion, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: needs_medication_management
per_column.rationale: Clean binary need axis. Samples align well with source (statin/beta-blocker, adapalene/doxycycline -> 1; viral URI supportive care -> 0).

per_column.name: needs_diagnostic_testing
per_column.rationale: Useful filter axis; sample values track ordered labs/MRI/echo correctly and absence where no tests mentioned.

per_column.name: needs_specialist_referral
per_column.rationale: Distinct binary axis. Sample rows all 0, consistent with no referral language; plausible reading.

per_column.name: needs_monitoring_followup
per_column.rationale: Useful axis; 'return if worse', 'repeat lipid panel', follow-up context support the 1s; grounded reads.

per_column.name: needs_lifestyle_counseling
per_column.rationale: Reasonable independent axis. The viral URI row is flagged 1 for lifestyle_counseling though 'supportive care advised' is not clearly lifestyle counseling -- a somewhat stretched inference, mildly reducing groundedness.

per_column.name: needs_mental_health
per_column.rationale: Rarer flag (17/250) but still a genuine analytical axis for a needs query; no contradicting samples observed, values look conservative.

per_column.name: needs_preventive_care
per_column.rationale: Valid axis. The annual physical row plausibly warranted preventive_care=1 but was coded 0; this is a miss rather than a fabrication, so groundedness only mildly affected.

per_column.name: needs_wound_skin_care
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis; acne row correctly flagged 1, others 0. Well grounded.

per_column.name: needs_physical_rehabilitation
per_column.rationale: Genuine axis for rehab needs; sample rows 0 consistent with text. Plausible.

judge.rationale: The added columns directly and richly address the query 'What patient needs appear in visit notes?': a multi-label extraction column, a complexity count, and one-hot indicators per need category all give strong axes to group, compare, and model. The one-hot columns are not merely redundant restatements because they enable per-need filtering/aggregation the concatenated string cannot easily support. Groundedness is generally good and conservative, with correct absence handling, but there is a recurring over-labelling issue (a false pain_management flag on the pain-denying annual physical, a stretched lifestyle_counseling flag on a viral URI), which caps groundedness below excellent. Overall a solid, useful, mostly well-grounded augmentation set.
